title: Chapter 92
content:
Given the man’s violent, possessive streak, Jakyeong had braced himself for Il-hyun to take a fillet knife to his back the moment they cleared the gates.

Instead, the corporate heir was disarmingly gentle.

Hovering over him in the master suite, Il-hyun meticulously checked every inch of Jakyeong's frame, disinfecting the reopened graze along his forearm before wrapping fresh sterile gauze around the muscle.

"You know you've been running around with a loose screw lately, darling?"

A sharp knot of indignant pride tightened in Jakyeong’s chest, but he couldn't find the breath to argue. Blown extraction, sloppy tactical awareness, dropping his sidearm—every single criticism was entirely justified.

"I'm sorry..."

"I didn't bring it up to fish for an apology," Il-hyun murmured, securing the medical tape. "I brought it up so you'd pull your head out of your ass and protect your own skin."

"..."

"Is your head in the clouds because of your brother?"

Jakyeong pressed his lips into a thin line, holding his tongue.

The hands smoothing the white gauze down his arm were impossibly tender—so delicate it was difficult to reconcile them with the fingers that had gouged a man's eyeball from its socket less than an hour ago. When Jakyeong looked up, their eyes locked, and Il-hyun offered a soft, radiant smile.

The distraction, the careless mistakes, the constant static fogging his focus... none of it was because of Wang Ryun.

Unable to lay his raw thoughts bare, Jakyeong simply mumbled that he wouldn't let his guard down again.

Finishing the dressing, Il-hyun placed a cigarette between his lips, struck a flame, took a slow drag, and passed the filter across. Jakyeong took it, exhaling a plume of gray smoke just as a sharp knock sounded at the door.

Park Tae-soo stepped inside. "Everything is prepared, President Kang."

Il-hyun rose to his full height, extending an open hand toward Jakyeong with the courtly, exaggerated grace of a gentleman escorting a date onto the ballroom floor.

"Shall we proceed, darling?"

An icy dread crawled down Jakyeong’s neck. No way. Surely he wouldn't...

"Don't be nervous," Il-hyun purred smoothly. "Tae-soo has an exceptionally delicate hand when it comes to raw sashimi."

Jakyeong nearly choked on his cigarette, his jaw slacking in pure disbelief. He wasn't joking?!

"Stop playing insane games."

"I am not a generous man, darling. I don't possess the charity to stomach another bastard sharing the exact same mark on your skin. You know this."

The jealousy was absurd. The coiled serpent wasn't just Takeya Jun's signature—half the underworld crews they ran with in Macau had inked the exact same design out of reckless bravado. Was the lunatic planning on hunting down every street operative across Asia?

Jakyeong tried to explain the syndicate context, but Il-hyun’s mind was already locked in total, unhinged tunnel vision.

"We will slice it clean off, and then I'll brand you with something to my personal liking."

"And... what the hell would that be?"

"A little kitten."

Hearing a terrifying syndicate boss declare he was going to carve a kitten into human flesh with a straight face sent a violent chill down Jakyeong's spine. The deadpan conviction made it terrifyingly clear the man wasn't bluffing.

When Il-hyun moved to haul him out of the chair, Jakyeong dug his heels into the hardwood with everything he had.

It took fifteen minutes of frantic, desperate bargaining to secure a compromise: the moment he returned from Hawaii, he would have the ink scrubbed with a professional medical laser.

"You're giving me your word," Il-hyun warned, his dark eyes narrowing into razor slits. "If that snake is still on your shoulder when you land, I'll carve it out with my own hands."

Jakyeong gave a sullen, begrudging nod, prompting Il-hyun to affectionately ruffle his dark bangs.

"Good boy. Look how sweet you are when you listen."

Jakyeong slapped the hand away with a venomous scowl. "Stop switching between playing the lunatic and playing the sweetheart! You look completely psychotic!"

Il-hyun put on an exaggerated, wounded pout, asking if his psychosis was truly that obvious.

Standing in the doorway, Park Tae-soo watched the bickering pair with a faint, almost imperceptible smirk of deep satisfaction. Jakyeong shot the security chief a dirty look. When your boss loses his goddamn mind, you're supposed to tackle him, not watch like a proud father.

Once Tae-soo excused himself, Jakyeong retreated to his own suite to pack.

He threw open his duffel bag on the rug, tossing in fresh clothes while Kang Il-hyun lounged on the edge of the mattress, resting his chin on his palm as he watched every movement.

"Need a hand, darling?"

"I'm fine. I'll pack the basics and buy the rest in Honolulu."

While folding a pair of trousers, a small, hard object tumbled from the fabric, rolling across the floorboards to bump against Il-hyun’s leather loafer.

Il-hyun bent down, plucking it from the floor.

Jakyeong’s stomach dropped. He lunged to snatch it back, but the man was a fraction of a second faster.

It was the hand-carved wooden elephant Il-hyun had gifted him in Macau—the trinket he had buried deep beneath his civilian clothes.

"Give it back," Jakyeong muttered, extending an open palm.

Il-hyun’s lips curved into a soft, fascinated smile. "I'm genuinely touched. I had no idea you treasured my little keepsake so deeply."

I stuffed it in a pocket and forgot about it, Jakyeong wanted to snap, but the words stuck in his throat.

"Hand it over. Now."

When Jakyeong reached for it, Il-hyun whipped the carved figurine behind his back, flashing a sleazy, roguish grin.

"I happen to own a significantly larger elephant. Would you care for an up-close demonstration?"

Judging by the wicked gleam behind those dark irises, that "larger elephant" was currently residing beneath his trousers. Sure enough, Il-hyun’s hand dropped to his belt buckle. Jakyeong snatched the wooden carving from behind the man's hip, shoved it into the bottom of his duffel, and pointedly turned his back.

Sliding off the mattress, Il-hyun settled onto the floor right beside him, deliberately sticking to his flank.

He began rummaging through the packed bag, pulling folded shirts loose and making an absolute nuisance of himself. Pushing him away was like shoving a brick wall; within seconds, Il-hyun was draping his heavy torso over Jakyeong’s shoulders, resting his cheek against the boy's collarbone.

"I'm going to miss you."

The quiet, unvarnished murmur cut straight through the playful banter.

It sounded more genuinely sincere than any grand declaration the man had ever made, leaving a sharp, tender ache behind Jakyeong’s ribs. Jakyeong stopped folding, his eyes drifting sideways.

Il-hyun’s heavy gaze burned into his profile.

Slowly, long fingers cupped the back of Jakyeong’s neck, pulling him into a soft, lingering kiss. Parting by a fraction of an inch, Il-hyun exhaled a thick, ragged breath against his lips.

"Fuck... My poor cock is doomed to a month of solitary confinement."

Right when things were getting sweet.

Jakyeong rolled his eyes, returning to his luggage, only for large, warm hands to slip beneath his shirt, tracing his ribs with persistent hunger. Resisting the hold felt utterly exhausting, and before Jakyeong could protest, the duffel was kicked aside, and the two were tumbling across the Persian rug in a tangled heap of heat and friction.

Just as Il-hyun captured his mouth again, a sharp knock rattled the door.

Park Tae-soo’s stoic baritone broke through the wood: "President Kang. An urgent matter requires your presence outside."

Il-hyun pressed one last, lingering peck to Jakyeong’s parted lips, adjusted his robe, and rose to his feet. When Jakyeong moved to follow, Il-hyun gave him a gentle push back onto the rug, telling him to finish packing before sliding the door shut.

Low, urgent murmurs drifted from the lounge before fading down the staircase. When Jakyeong finally stepped into the corridor, Kang Il-hyun had already vanished from the estate.

"The house is going to feel dreadfully empty without you, Master Ja-kyeong."

Setting out the breakfast spread, the senior housekeeper wore a sorrowful frown. Jakyeong privately lamented that he wouldn't get to taste her incredible home cooking for an entire month.

While picking at his eggs, he casually fished for information regarding Il-hyun's whereabouts, only for the housekeeper to look over his shoulder with a warm, knowing smile.

"Why not ask him yourself?"

Jakyeong turned around, startled.

Standing in the arched doorway in a crisp, charcoal three-piece suit was Kang Il-hyun, watching him with an amused smirk. He pulled out the adjacent chair and sat down.

While the housekeeper poured fresh coffee, Il-hyun’s eyes drifted over Jakyeong’s attire. Accustomed to seeing the boy in drab, tactical blacks and grays, the vibrant crimson Hawaiian floral shirt looked stunningly striking on his frame.

"Well, well. Look at this magnificent outfit."

"It's one of my favorites," Jakyeong muttered defensively.

"You should wear it more often."

I would, if my job didn't require me to blend into the dark.

"Does it look ridiculous?"

"Not at all. It complements those delinquent, feral eyes of yours perfectly."

Jakyeong narrowed his eyes into razor slits, aggressively chewing his toast until his cheeks puffed out.

Finding the display endlessly endearing, Il-hyun reached out, poking Jakyeong’s full cheek with his index finger.

"Where is your eldest brother?"

"He packed his bags early and headed over to the hospital."

The Hawaiian retreat wasn't just for the three operatives; Il-hyun had arranged for a private medical team and security detail to accompany Wang Ryun overseas to ensure his recovery was undisturbed. The quiet, meticulous consideration the man extended behind the scenes didn't go unnoticed.

Tearing a piece of toast, Jakyeong casually broached last night's emergency, curious why Tae-soo had pulled him away.

"A corporate fire broke out at one of the subsidiaries," Il-hyun said smoothly. "I had to handle the cleanup."

"I see..."

"A transport team will escort you to Incheon International. I have an executive board briefing, so I need to head to headquarters shortly."

"What about Jun?"

"The Japanese contractor?"

Jakyeong gave a slow nod. Il-hyun reached across the linen, brushing a stray crumb from the corner of Jakyeong’s lip with a tranquil smile.

"Don't worry your pretty head, darling. He's been properly handled and buried six feet under the dirt."

Did he turn him into dog food again? Takeya Jun was far too slippery and dangerous a predator to go down easily, but seeing the calm assurance in Il-hyun's eyes, Jakyeong pushed the worry down. Ever since they met, Kang Il-hyun had surpassed Wang Han as the single person who touched his hair the most.

Long fingers trailed down his cheek, brushing the shell of his ear, tracing the slope of his neck and shoulder before reluctantly pulling away.

The lingering absence of that warmth left a cold, hollow ache.

Before Jakyeong could process the feeling, the scrape of a chair echoed through the dining room as Il-hyun stood up.

"Take good care of yourself, darling. Call me the second your wheels touch down in Honolulu."

Stepping behind Jakyeong’s chair, Il-hyun leaned down, planting a firm, affectionate kiss on his flushed cheek. Clearing the dishes nearby, the housekeeper giggled into her apron. Jakyeong sat frozen, his ears burning a violent, feverish crimson.

Offering a polite parting remark to the staff, Il-hyun strode out toward the motorcade.

Watching the tailored back retreat with such casual indifference, a sudden, bitter swell of disappointment tightened in Jakyeong’s chest.

A whole month apart... and he acts like he's just popping out for groceries.

Am I the only idiot agonizing over this?

Jakyeong stared down at the untouched porcelain cup before him. Il-hyun hadn't taken a single sip of his coffee—spending the entire breakfast simply staring at Jakyeong’s face before walking away.

As he bit down on his lower lip in quiet turmoil, his phone vibrated against the table.

It was Wang Han.

[Did you leave the estate yet?] Han’s voice crackled through the receiver, ragged and out of breath.

"Not yet. Why are you panting like that?"

[Did you know about this, Wei?]

"Know about what?"

[Jun. He broke custody and escaped while Il-hyun's security detail was transferring him last night.]

Jakyeong nearly dropped the handset.

His head snapped toward the grand foyer. Without thinking, his legs moved on pure instinct, sprinting through the double doors and out onto the front drive, the phone still pressed to his ear.

[I only caught wind of it from the estate guards at the hospital,] Han rushed out. [They've been tearing the city apart since dawn trying to lock the perimeter down.]

Jakyeong skidded to a halt in the center of the gravel courtyard.

Down by the main gates, Kang Il-hyun was trading final instructions with Park Tae-soo. Catching the hurried footsteps, Il-hyun looked back over his shoulder.

Jakyeong locked his fists tight, his dark eyes drilling into the corporate heir.

Why did you lie to me? You said he was dead. You told me not to worry.

Through the receiver, Han let out a heavy, defeated sigh.

[With a shattered wrist and an empty eye socket, even Takeya Jun won't last long on the run.]

"..."

[Wei? Are you there?]

"Yeah..."

[Hurry over to the hospital. Ryun is asking for you.]

Jakyeong didn't answer, ending the call with a curt tap.

He marched straight across the gravel toward the black armored sedan, his hand shooting out to clamp firmly onto Kang Il-hyun’s tailored forearm.

Il-hyun looked down at the grip on his sleeve, then lifted his dark gaze to meet Jakyeong’s blazing eyes.

"To what do I owe this sudden, passionate display, darling?"

"I'm not going."

Il-hyun’s brow arched into a sharp, quizzical peak.

Jakyeong held the man's stare with unyielding, fierce conviction. "I'm not getting on that plane to Hawaii. I'm staying right here."

Il-hyun’s eyes narrowed slightly, searching the boy's face in genuine confusion.

Jakyeong parted his lips. The words had to be said. If he boarded that flight in silence, his chest would implode with suffocating regret. Whether he died of mortification or died in a firefight, he was past the point of caring.

"I'm staying..." Jakyeong rasped, his voice trembling with raw, desperate resolve. "...to protect you."

Il-hyun blinked, utter bewilderment washing over his handsome features.

"Protect... who?"

Jakyeong bit the inside of his cheek, abandoning the last shred of his dignity.

Ah, fuck it all.

"You, President Kang! I'm staying to protect your psychotic ass!"

The patronizing amusement instantly drained from Kang Il-hyun’s face.

His expression shifted into something entirely new—a look Jakyeong had never witnessed in their entire history together. Not during their violent nights tangled in bed, not when a severed head was dumped at his feet, and not when he was carving human bone with a combat blade.

It was a look of pure, unadulterated, breathless reverence.
